title: Computer Science Fundamentals: Practical Core for Builders
summary: A hands-on 4-week foundation in practical computer science essentials. Master data structures, algorithmic complexity, system memory, networking, and concurrency to write efficient and robust software.

days.title: Binary, Hexadecimal, and Data Encoding
objectives: Convert numbers between decimal, binary, and hexadecimal formats
Calculate byte sizes for integer and UTF-8 encoded text payloads

days.title: Stack vs Heap Memory Layout
objectives: Differentiate variable allocation between stack frames and heap space
Predict memory leak risks by tracing variable lifetimes

days.title: Time and Space Complexity with Big-O
objectives: Determine the time complexity of simple loops and nested loops
Calculate auxiliary space consumed by iterative algorithms

days.title: Contiguous Memory: Arrays and Dynamic Resizing
objectives: Compute amortized cost for dynamic array appending operations
Explain CPU cache locality benefits of contiguous arrays over fragmented pointers

days.title: Pointer-Based Structures: Singly and Doubly Linked Lists
objectives: Trace insertion and deletion operations in linked lists step-by-step
Choose between dynamic arrays and linked lists given specific read/write access patterns

days.title: LIFO and FIFO: Stacks, Queues, and Deques
objectives: Implement a FIFO queue using array or linked node backends
Trace stack operations to validate matching pairs of parentheses in expressions

days.title: Hash Tables and Collision Resolution
objectives: Explain how hash collisions occur and how separate chaining resolves them
Calculate load factors to decide when hash tables require resizing

days.title: Recursion and Call Stack Limits
objectives: Identify the base case and recursive relation in recursive functions
Diagnose and prevent stack overflow conditions in deeply recursive routines

days.title: Divide and Conquer: Binary Search and Sorting
objectives: Implement binary search on sorted data to achieve logarithmic search time
Compare merge sort and quicksort tradeoffs in terms of worst-case time and space

days.title: Hierarchical Data: Binary Search Trees (BST)
objectives: Trace in-order, pre-order, and post-order traversals of a binary tree
Explain how an unbalanced binary search tree degrades lookup performance to linear time

days.title: Graph Representations: Adjacency Matrix vs List
objectives: Model network topologies using adjacency list representations
Compare storage footprints of dense versus sparse graph representations

days.title: Graph Traversal: BFS vs DFS
objectives: Trace breadth-first search to find the shortest path in unweighted graphs
Trace depth-first search to detect cycles within a directed graph

days.title: Operating System Basics: Processes, Threads, and Context Switching
objectives: Contrast process memory isolation with thread shared-memory models
Explain the computational overhead involved in operating system context switches

days.title: Concurrency Challenges: Race Conditions and Deadlocks
objectives: Identify critical sections prone to data race conditions in multithreaded logic
Recognize the four conditions necessary for deadlock to arise

days.title: File Systems, Persistent Storage, and I/O Latency
objectives: Compare latency differences between L1/L2 CPU cache, RAM, NVMe SSD, and disk
Explain why buffering and batching reduce I/O bottlenecks in data operations

days.title: Networking Core: IP Addressing, DNS, and Routing
objectives: Explain how DNS resolves domain names into routable IP addresses
Trace a data packet routing step through subnets and gateways

days.title: Transport Layer: TCP Three-Way Handshake vs UDP
objectives: Diagram the TCP three-way handshake and connection termination flow
Select appropriately between TCP and UDP based on reliability and latency requirements

days.title: Application Layer: HTTP/HTTPS Lifecycle and Headers
objectives: Trace an HTTP request/response exchange including status codes and headers
Explain how TLS handshakes establish encrypted communication channels

days.title: Caching Mechanisms: LRU Cache and Invalidation
objectives: Combine a hash table and doubly linked list to design a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache
Identify common cache invalidation strategies and trade-offs

days.title: End-to-End System Design: What Happens When You Request a URL
objectives: Trace the full lifecycle of a web request from browser input through network stacks to server disk
Diagnose system performance bottlenecks across compute, memory, and network boundaries
